  WHY: If the marker write succeeds but tg_send_msg fails, the alerted status is recorded as 1. Subsequent sweep ticks will read this marker, see alerted=1, and suppress the alert permanently, resulting in a silent failure to page for a conflicted PR that should have alerted.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26454-26467 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_standalone_conflict_count_attempt` persists `alerted="1"` before sending the Telegram warning, and a failed send is swallowed.
  WHY: The persisted marker makes the next sweep short-circuit without retrying; `tg_send_msg` in `scripts/tg_helpers.sh` returns success-without-message-id when the level is filtered, credentials are missing, or the request fails.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26460 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: There is no test for “marker write succeeded but Telegram send failed”.
  WHY: Existing tests only assert `sends == []` when `gh` returns 1, never when `gh` returns 0 but Telegram fails.
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: "Telegram now pages only when a person has to act." The default `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL` threshold moves from `DEBUG` to `WARNING`, so the stuck-conflict WARNING must actually reach Telegram when its threshold trips.
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh `_standalone_conflict_count_attempt` and the new `tests/test_alert_levels_human_only.py` test cases.
  Evidence of absence: The LAST RUN reorders the function to write the marker first, then send the Telegram, with `tg_send_msg ... || true` swallowing any send failure. There is no test that simulates "marker PATCH succeeds, Telegram send fails" to prove the page is not lost. The README's `STANDALONE_CONFLICT_STUCK_ALERT_ATTEMPTS` row (line 257) documents `outcome=write_failed` only; it does not cover the telegram-loss path the new ordering creates. Without a guard or second write, a head that is genuinely stuck may never page an operator.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26454-26467 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_standalone_conflict_count_attempt` persists `alerted=1` before attempting the Telegram send and never retries when delivery fails.
  WHY: After the threshold is reached, a successful marker write stores `alerted=1`; if Telegram rejects or fails the send, the error is swallowed. `tg_send_msg` also returns success without a message ID when its `curl` call fails (`scripts/tg_helpers.sh`, lines 124-133). Later sweeps read `alerted=1` and skip the warning, so the stuck PR never pages a person.
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: “The GitHub rate-limit alert (`gh_helpers.sh`) is now `DEBUG`” and “README: … the alert-level text of the re-leveled features.”
  Expected change site: README.md, “GitHub API rate-limit admin alert” example.
  Evidence of absence: The example at line 3281 still labels the alert `⚠️ WARNING`, while the implementation and README description at lines 3298-3300 say it is `DEBUG`.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: “Pool health when accounts are only gated. A rejected token or a failed probe stays `WARNING`.”
  Expected change site: README.md, `CLAUDE_POOL_HEALTH_ALERT_ENABLED` row and “Near-cap alert” section; `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`, pool-health step comment.
  Evidence of absence: The README row at line 2351 and near-cap description at lines 2770-2775 say the alert is `WARNING` for accounts at the usage gate without distinguishing gated-only accounts from rejected tokens or failed probes. The workflow comment at lines 876-878 likewise describes a generic `WARNING`. None reflects the implemented `DEBUG` level for gated-only accounts and `WARNING` for rejected tokens or failed probes.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26453-26468 (_standalone_conflict_count_attempt, alert branch) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The counter persists `alerted=1` into the marker comment before the Telegram WARNING is sent, and the send is fire-and-forget (`tg_send_msg ... || true`).
  WHY: If the Telegram call fails after the marker PATCH succeeded, later sweeps find `alerted=1` and never re-send; the last run's fix only moved the send after the marker write and did not close the send-failure window.
- TASK_GAP:

One re-leveled feature is the GitHub rate-limit alert: "`gh_helpers.sh` is now `DEBUG`".
  Expected change site: README.md, "GitHub API rate-limit admin alert" example block (~line 3281).
  Evidence of absence: README.md:3281 still shows the example `⚠️ WARNING: GitHub API rate limit hit — workflow=<name> repo=<owner/repo> run=<runs-url>`, while the actual alert now emits `🔍 DEBUG: GitHub API rate limit hit` (scripts/gh_helpers.sh:490) and the `TG_GH_RATELIMIT_ALERT_COOLDOWN_SECS` row at README.md:298 was updated to describe the DEBUG level. No diff hunk updates the stale example, so README contradicts both the code and its own variable row.
  SEVERITY: NIT

  Requirement: PR description, Docs section: README must include "the alert-level text of the re-leveled features." The pool-health feature was re-leveled: "Pool health when accounts are only gated" moved to DEBUG, with rejected tokens / failed probes staying WARNING (Q1/Q4 operator decisions).
  Expected change site: README.md `CLAUDE_POOL_HEALTH_ALERT_ENABLED` row (line 2351) and the "Near-cap alert" prose (lines 2767-2783); also the step comment in .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:876-878.

All three describe the pre-PR behavior. scripts/claude_pool_health_alert.sh:88-92 now sends `DEBUG` for gated-only pools and `WARNING` only when `auth_failed>0` or `probe_failed>0`. docs/INVENTORY.md:143 and agents.md:2159 ("one Telegram WARNING named every account...") carry the same stale text.
